answer: Each identity must hold one registered charity trusteeship, checked live against the sable charity registry: one trusteeship backs exactly one identity, and a second identity citing the same seat is rejected. A fake needs a real charity, a board vote and a 60-day vetting window, costing 1,500 units in fees; 100 fakes need 150,000 units, 6,000 days and 100 separate atlas entries. Cheapest cheat: buy a dormant charity shell — pricier than forming one, the seller surrenders their own seat, and the opal registry flags rapid trustee churn. Linked charities expose clusters under one controller.
